recentItems.title: Russia-Ukraine talks end with prisoner exchange agreement in Abu Dhabi
recentItems.description:
Russia and Ukraine have agreed to a large-scale prisoner exchange following two days of US-mediated peace talks in Abu Dhabi, although the number of prisoners involved has yet to be confirmed.

US envoy Jared Kushner described the negotiations as a productive first step, saying progress had been made on security guarantees, ceasefire monitoring and post-war arrangements. He said he and Steve Witkoff would travel to Moscow to brief Russian President Vladimir Putin before meeting Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Dublin.

But major disagreements remain over territory, particularly Russia's demands concerning the Donbas region. The discussions also highlighted calls to include European countries in future negotiations, as questions remain over Ukraine's post-war security.

Al Jazeera's Dmitri Medvedenko reports from Abu Dhabi.

recentItems.title: Gaza Grad: A Palestinian-Russian family’s longing for home | Al Jazeera World Documentary
recentItems.description:
Forced from Gaza, a Palestinian-Russian family rebuilds their lives across Russia and Egypt, longing to return home.

When war engulfs Gaza in October 2023, members of a Palestinian-Russian family hold on for as long as they can. They have a route out of the Strip. But Anna and Ghassan Ashour and their daughters, Lisa and Donia, stay on despite the worsening conditions, because Gaza is their home. But as the violence escalates, they’re eventually forced to leave and head to Russia in search of safety. For Lisa and Donia, life there is unfamiliar. Struggling with the language, culture and separation from Gaza, the two of them move to Egypt, closer to home and to the possibility of a return. Split between Russia and Egypt, the family must find new ways to live with distance, uncertainty and longing. Their story reveals the enduring tension between the need for safety and the place that they still think of as home.
